reviews.comment: The worst. Don't take her. Got her bad reviews taken down.

SOCI 337 
It's a lot of reading but it's interesting and I'm now aware of much more contemporary racism. Participation is really important but you can always write for that. The grading was harsh with little feedback but that was her TA grading not her, so a different TA will have a different result. Discussion based, I'm taking her other class!

Dr. Kim is truly a very sweet and caring person. She is passionate about environmental justice and issues regarding marginalized people groups. I certainly learned a lot in her International Immigration course. It was fun and engaging. If you don't mind a little bit of a reading load, you will be fine!

She's not given enough credit imo. There may be quite a bit of reading, but so long as you do it, you should be fine. There's one group project, one essay, and lots of journal/discussion boards.
Other than that, she allows half a page of written notes for her midterm and final and cares about what she teaches and her students.

reviews.comment: I loved this class! Earning an A isn't hard, but u have to earn it. Lots of extra credit. Office hours helped when I didn't understand. You DON'T have to speak for participation. Exams came straight from the guides. The journals/posts were easy but req reading. Prof Kim was super caring & knowledgeable. Def recommend if u care about ur education!

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER. She is a smart person but not a good professor. Her rubric for all assignments are not clear, so she can grade harshly. Attendance is mandatory and she makes you take notes on paper not computer. We are paying for this class we should take notes how we want. She grades participation which is hard and unfair in a 50 person class.

Takes A MONTH to grade assignments with two TA's. Final grades were posted last minute and then she created an automated email response so that you can't reach her. Just does not seem to care about students. An A shouldn't be easy, but it shouldn't feel like not even your best work deserves an A, which is how her class feels.

These negative reviews likely come from students who just wanted an easy A without putting in any work. She is incredibly wealthy with knowledge in her field, so of course, she uses her book as a source to teach from. If you really want to get something out of the education you or your parents pay thousands of dollars for, take her class.

reviews.comment: She is a great professor, her syllabus is a bit confusing and she babbles the whole class which can be very boring, her class is very easy. To get participation points just raise your hand and add on to subject. 8 journals and 4 discussion posts throughout the semester which is very easy.Books are all free.Exam questions straight from study guide.

I am sure Ms. Kim is a good person, but I truly hope she changes her grading after taking her class. She is never able to get through her lectures, grades participation so harshly that you will likely never get above a 70. I was taking this class for some boring international credit and ended up with a gpa killer. Thank you for nothing!!

Worst prof l've ever had. Searches for ways to take points off of your grace.
Uses textbook she wrote. Course was narrow minded. Participation grade is based off of how much eye contact you make with the prof. Unclear rubrics. No multiple choice so everything is written making it incredibly hard to give the answer she is looking for.

Terrible. Syllabus is very unclear, takes off points without explanation or because rubrics were not clear and then her and the TA gaslight you if you bring it up to them. Took literally a month to get grades back on some of my assignments. It felt like she didn't care about our success. Biased lectures that we could never finish.

Seems like a nice person but not a great professor. You are graded on participation by speaking in class, but this class had 60 students. So each person getting a good participation grade is nearly impossible. The content in class was interesting but she seemed to only cover a small portion of important content each class because of participation.
